name: single-mutation phenotypic neighborhood
verbatim_definition: the set of phenotypes that are accessible from a given genotype by a single point mutation
math: N_P(g) = { phi(g') : d_genome(g,g') = 1 }, where phi is the genotype-phenotype map. Companion genetic neighborhood N_G(g) = { g' : d_genome(g,g') = 1 } ('the set of all genomes different in one position from the wild type genomes').
computational_cost: exactly B evaluations per genome for a binary genome of length B (B=104 circuits, B=76 RNA); linear in genome length, embarrassingly parallel
sensitivity: resolves which phenotypes are one step away and how far they are in phenotype space; detects stocking of the neighborhood with specific previously-rewarded phenotypes
what_it_sees: the local adjacent possible under the system's ACTUAL variation operator, in phenotype space rather than genotype space
what_it_cannot_see: anything reachable only by 2+ mutations or by recombination; the crossover operator was active (P_c=0.5 in circuits) but the neighborhood is defined over point mutation only, so the measured neighborhood is NOT the full offspring distribution of the actual algorithm
known_confounds: requires a phenotype distance metric and a definition of 'useful'; both are supplied by the experimenter and both encode the authored decomposition
portability_to_SFE: HIGH. Requires only (a) a discrete genome, (b) an enumerable 1-mutant set, (c) a phenotype equality/distance test. Prometheus symbolic organisms satisfy all three.
d_level_supported: D1 alone; D2 when computed over a population

name: facilitated variation (FV) measure
verbatim_definition: The 'quantity' component is the probability of forming a potentially useful phenotype which is novel by a single point mutation; the 'quality' component is the average phenotypic distance between the wild-type and the potentially useful phenotypes within its phenotypic neighborhood. This measure is then normalized for its corresponding value with respect to non-useful neighboring phenotypes.
math: FV = [ P(useful novel | 1 mutation) * mean_d(useful, wildtype) ] / [ P(non-useful | 1 mutation) * mean_d(non-useful, wildtype) ]. Exact algebra is in Text S1 section 8.1, WHICH WAS NOT RECOVERED - treat the reconstruction as INFERRED.
computational_cost: same as DET-MVG-01 plus a usefulness classifier per neighbor
sensitivity: rises measurably over generations under both FG and MVG, significantly faster under MVG; decays rapidly when the environment is made constant
what_it_sees: a scalar summary of neighborhood quality that can be tracked as a TRAJECTORY, which is what makes longitudinal (D3) accessibility measurement possible at all
what_it_cannot_see: direction. FV is a scalar; it does not say WHICH dimensions became accessible, so it cannot distinguish broadening from re-aiming
known_confounds: CRITICAL - 'useful' is defined as 'phenotypes with the same modular structure', i.e. the metric is defined relative to the experimenter's decomposition. FV is therefore NOT a neutral evolvability measure; it measures alignment to the authored basis. A system that became broadly more evolvable along orthogonal directions would score LOW. This is the single most important caveat in this file.
portability_to_SFE: MEDIUM. The trajectory design is portable; the usefulness predicate must be replaced by something not authored by the same hand that authored the world, or the measure is tautological (cf. feedback_neutrality_gate_can_be_tautological).
d_level_supported: D3 when plotted against generation over a population

name: intra-module vs inter-module mutational effect (pleiotropy decomposition)
verbatim_definition: normalized phenotypic effect of mutations within their own module versus on other modules
math: for each mutation, measure phenotypic change restricted to the module containing the mutated locus (intra) and to all other modules (inter). Circuits: compared over the series of gate outputs within each module across all input combinations. RNA: over subsequences.
measured_values: circuits FG 0.12+-0.002 vs MVG 0.14+-0.001 (intra, p<1e-4); FG 0.04+-0.005 vs MVG 0.01+-0.001 (inter, p<1e-4). RNA FG 0.28+-0.007 vs MVG 0.36+-0.005 (intra, p<1e-9); FG 0.057+-0.005 vs MVG 0.053+-0.005 (inter, NOT SIGNIFICANT).
what_it_sees: whether variation respects module boundaries - the mechanical signature of a restructured variation operator
what_it_cannot_see: whether the module partition it uses is the right one; the partition is supplied
known_confounds: requires a module assignment. In the source the assignment comes from the authored goal decomposition, so the detector confirms alignment to the author's partition by construction. Substrate-dependent: the pleiotropy leg FAILED to reach significance in RNA.
portability_to_SFE: MEDIUM-LOW. Needs a defensible module partition that is not authored by the world designer. Consider deriving the partition from the organism (e.g. by graph clustering) rather than from the goal.

name: genetic trigger detector (mutual information with environment)
verbatim_definition: The genetic triggers can thus be detected by evaluating the mutual information between the environment (goal) and the genomic content at each position ... Trigger positions were readily detected for all MVG cases tested.
math: per-locus I(goal ; genome_content_at_locus) over the population time series; triggers are the argmax loci
computational_cost: trivial - one MI estimate per locus over recorded run history
sensitivity: found triggers in ALL MVG cases tested in circuits; in RNA 'mutual information is spread amongst' many positions rather than concentrated
what_it_sees: which loci carry information about the current environment - i.e. where the environmental memory is physically stored
what_it_cannot_see: whether those loci are CAUSALLY responsible. The source never perturbs them. This detector produces a hypothesis, not a mechanism.
known_confounds: MI on sparse histograms is biased upward (cf. feedback_mi_bias) - a random-pairing null is required and the source does not report one. Argmax over loci is an order statistic (cf. ATTACK_PATTERNS order-statistic scaling): the top-MI locus of a null genome is not zero, and no null distribution over loci is reported.
portability_to_SFE: HIGH, and it is the natural handle for the missing D5 perturbation: identify triggers by MI, then knock them out.
d_level_supported: D0 by itself - it is a localisation instrument, not an accessibility instrument

name: normalized network modularity Q_m
verbatim_definition: Q over K modules with L edges, l_s within-module edges and d_s summed node degree per module s; normalized as Q_m using Q_rand from degree-preserving randomizations and a Q_max term
math: Q_m = (Q_real - Q_rand)/(Q_max - Q_rand); Q_rand averaged over 1,000 degree-preserving randomized networks
measured_values: circuits FG 0.12+-0.02, MVG 0.54+-0.02; neural FG 0.15+-0.02, MVG 0.35+-0.02; reference scale nonmodular ~0, modular 0.3-1
what_it_sees: a STATE VARIABLE of network structure
what_it_cannot_see: anything about future acquisition. This is the detector most often mistaken for an evolvability measure. 2007 Table 1 shows randomly varying goals give large speedups while 2005 shows they give NO modularity - so Q_m and adaptation speed dissociate.
known_confounds: requires a partition (modularity maximisation is itself an argmax over partitions, with a known resolution limit); degree-preserving null is the right null and IS used here
portability_to_SFE: HIGH for graph-structured organisms, MEANINGLESS for organisms without a natural edge set

name: network motif significance profile
math: Z = (N_real - N_rand)/sigma per 3- and 4-node subgraph, over all such subgraphs
known_confounds: multiple comparison across all 3- and 4-node subgraphs with no correction reported; motif counts are strongly driven by degree sequence
portability_to_SFE: LOW - requires a graph substrate and adds little that Q_m does not for this question

name: non-evolved phenotype-matched control construction
source: Parter, Kashtan & Alon 2008, Fig 9B/9C and Text S1 section 3.1
verbatim_definition: a random class of inverse-fold genomes (genomes generated by an algorithm to yield a desired fold) ... circuits which achieve the goal but were generated by an optimization algorithm rather than by an evolutionary process
math: not a metric - a CONTROL DESIGN. Produce genomes with the target phenotype by non-evolutionary search (simulated annealing for circuits, inverse fold for RNA), then measure the same detector on them.
sample_sizes: 200 random RNA genomes; circuit count not stated in retrieved text
what_it_sees: separates 'is a solution to the goal' from 'arrived at the goal through a history'
what_it_cannot_see: does not separate structure from history, because the controls are not matched on modularity
portability_to_SFE: HIGH and STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. This is the cheapest available defence against the objection that any measured structural property is just a consequence of task success. Prometheus should adopt it as standing practice for every accessibility claim.
d_level_supported: control design, raises the credibility of any D-level
